extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and applicants using the EPO as ISA/IPEA in the PCT procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and search of PCT international applications where the EPO acts as International Searching/Examining Authority, covering abstracts, title, description, sufficiency, and claims requirements. Intended to direct examiners (and inform applicants) on form, content and objections under Arts. 5 and 6 and relevant Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: published abstract when search report published later
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search report is published later than the application, the abstract published with the application will be the one resulting from the procedure referred to in ISPE Guidelines 15.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure does not apply to supplementary international searches for which the EPO is SISA because the main ISA has already provided the publication data. See also ISPE Guidelines 16.36 and GL/PCT-EPO B-X, 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract content requirements are given in ISPE Guidelines 16.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO B-X, 7 for cross-reference. The content of the abstract is transmitted to the applicant together with the search report (Form PCT/ISA/210, Box IV). Applicant comments on the abstract are handled per ISPE Guidelines 16.40-16.43.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure accompanying the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for figures accompanying the abstract follow Section F-II, 2.4 in the EPO Guidelines for Examination, applied mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO B-X, 7 and ISPE Guidelines 16.37(c),(e) and 16.48-16.51 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist for considering the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the checklist in Annex 1 to Section F-II in the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO (applies mutatis mutandis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO F-II, 2.5 and related cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title must be short and precise
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 5.1(a) stipulates that the description 'shall first state the title of the invention as appearing in the request'. The title must be short and precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should review the title in the light of the description and claims and any amendments thereto to ensure the title, as well as being concise, gives a clear and adequate indication of the subject of the invention. If amendments change categories of claims, the examiner should check whether a corresponding amendment in the title is needed, not going beyond the disclosure in the application as filed. See ISPE Guidelines 16.44-16.47 and GL/PCT-EPO B-X, 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: recommended subheadings and formal structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The usage of the subheadings outlined in Section 204 of the Administrative Instructions under the PCT is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section F-II, 4.1 of the EPO Guidelines for Examination applies mutatis mutandis; include technical field, background art, technical problem and solution, references to drawings, reference signs, and other standard subheadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical field and background art in description
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical field should be indicated (see ISPE Guidelines 4.04) and background art should be presented following ISPE Guidelines 4.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPO applies option GL/ISPE A4.05[1] of Appendix to Chapter 4. Format and examples of background art citations are given in F-II, 4.3.1 and subparts for non-patent and patent literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrelevant matter should be avoided in the description
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrelevant matter should not be included in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section F-II, 4.4 in the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO applies mutatis mutandis. See also GL/PCT-EPO F-II, 7.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical problem and its solution must be explained
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should set out the technical problem and its solution (see ISPE Guidelines 4.06-4.07).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO F-II, 4.5 and related cross-references for examiners to assess disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to drawings and reference signs in description
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should include appropriate references to the drawings and use of reference signs as per ISPE Guidelines 4.08-4.09.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO F-II, 4.6-4.7 for details and for consistency with claims (reference signs in claims may create lack of clarity if used improperly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability must be indicated where not obvious
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should indicate explicitly the way in which the invention is capable of exploitation in industry, if this is not obvious from the description or nature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corresponds to 'susceptible of industrial application' and usually will be self-evident; exceptions include some testing methods and certain biotechnological inventions (e.g., sequences) where industrial application must be disclosed. See GL/PCT-EPO, G-III and GL/ISPE A14.01[2].1(1) and A14.01[2].2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and order of presentation; terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should observe proper manner and order of presentation (ISPE Guidelines 4.21) and consistent terminology (ISPE Guidelines 4.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirements under Rule 5.1(b) and Section 204 PCT AI apply; see GL/PCT-EPO F-II, 4.9-4.10 and GL/ISPE cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer programs and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Special guidance for computer programs is provided (see ISPE Guidelines 4.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 10.1(a),(b),(d),(e) and related GL/PCT-EPO references apply; software-related disclosure should follow those sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical values and units must follow recognised standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical values and units must be given properly (see GL/ISPE 4.24 and GL/EPO F-II, Annex 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use units recognised in international practice (Annex 2 to Section F-II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: form and content; photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must follow ISPE Guidelines 4.28; photographs are allowed only exceptionally, must be black and white on A4, respect margins and permit direct reproduction; colour drawings/photographs are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 11.10-11.13, PCT Receiving Office Guidelines Chapter VI, paragraph 146 (GL/RO 146), and F-II, 5.3 applied mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide and amino acid sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings must follow ISPE Guidelines 4.15 and Euro-PCT Guide points 157-160; non-compliant listings handled per GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII and C-VIII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to sequences disclosed in a database follows F-II, 6.1 applied mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions and matter not to be used
rubrics_metrics.description: There are categories of expressions which should not be contained in an international application as specified in Rule 9.1 and ISPE Guidelines 4.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes expressions/drawings contrary to morality or public order, disparaging statements, irrelevant matter and omission of matter from publication. See GL/PCT-EPO G-II,4.1 and other cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure: general requirement (Art.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed description of at least one way of carrying out the invention must be given so that a person skilled in the art can put the invention into practice; description must disclose any feature essential for carrying out the invention in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single example may suffice, but broad claim coverage normally requires multiple examples or alternative embodiments covering the claimed area. The skilled person must be able to perform the invention over the whole area claimed without undue burden and without needing inventive skill. For Art.5 objections, serious doubts must be substantiated by verifiable facts. See GL/ISPE 5.45-5.51 and GL/PCT-EPO F-III cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency vs additional subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of sufficiency must be balanced against the prohibition of introducing additional subject-matter; see ISPE Guidelines 4.12 for interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is only sufficiently disclosed for part of the claimed matter, examiners may invite informal clarification before search. See GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII, 3.3-3.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for ability to perform and repeat the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are serious doubts about the possibility of performing and repeating the invention as described, the burden of proof that it can be performed or that success is credible rests with the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant can discharge this burden during PCT Chapter II or after entry into the European phase before the EPO. See GL/PCT-EPO F-III, 3 and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial insufficiency cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where only variants of the invention are incapable of being performed, absence of well-known details, or general difficulties in performing the invention are treated under partial insufficiency rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See F-III, 5.1-5.3 applied mutatis mutandis and GL/PCT-EPO cross-references (e.g., G-VII, 5.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological material: deposit and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules apply to inventions relating to biological material, including deposit requirements and public availability under Rule 13bis and ISPE Guidelines 4.16-4.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Euro-PCT Guide points 150-156 for deposit handling and OJ EPO 2010, 498 for public availability; F-III,6.2 and 6.3 apply mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference documents and incorporation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reference documents relate to background art, they may be introduced later, but incorporation of essential matter or essential features at a later date is subject to restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may request the applicant to furnish documents necessary for a meaningful search. See GL/PCT-EPO F-II, 4.3 and H-II, 2.2.1 and 2.2.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency when parts were withdrawn from publication (R.20.5(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets stamped 'Not to be considered (R. 20.5(e) or 20.7)' do not form part of the application and must be ignored for search/examination; examiner must evaluate whether invention is still sufficiently disclosed without relying on withdrawn parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements of Art.5 are not satisfied without withdrawn parts, a corresponding objection is raised. See GL/PCT-EPO F-III, 3-5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between sufficiency (Art.5) and clarity (Art.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ambiguity in the claims may lead to an insufficiency objection only if the whole scope of the claim is affected so that it is impossible to carry out the invention; otherwise ambiguity is generally a clarity issue under Art.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisive is whether an ill-defined parameter prevents the skilled person from identifying technical measures necessary to solve the problem without undue burden. See GL/ISPE 4.12,5.58 and GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: mandatory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must contain 'one or more claims.' The claims must (i) 'define the matter for which protection is sought;' (ii) 'be clear and concise;' and (iii) 'be fully supported by the description.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art.3(2), Art.6 and GL/ISPE 5.01-5.02 govern claims. This chapter sets out form/content and interpretation for novelty/inventive step assessment and prior art searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of claims: technical features and functional features
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims' features should be technical; not every feature must be expressed structurally — functional features are acceptable where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See F-IV,2.1 and GL/ISPE 5.04. Functional features are further dealt with in GL/PCT-EPO F-IV, 6.5; specific cases (e.g., functional definition of pathological condition) are addressed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part form of claim drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, use the two-part form for claims (see ISPE Guidelines 5.05 and 5.22); there are cases where two-part form is unsuitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 6.3(b) and ISPE Guidelines 5.06-5.08 give guidance on when two-part form is required or unsuitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of claim and number/arrangement of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be of different categories; plural independent claims in one category complying with unity of invention may nonetheless be objected to under Art.6 if they result in lack of clarity or conciseness. Claims should be arranged logically (broadest first recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 5.12-5.19, Rules 6.4 and 11.10, and GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,3.2 and 4 for examples. Multiple dependent claims are allowed provided they do not detract from clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims directed to computer-implemented inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Special guidance applies to claims directed to computer-implemented inventions, distinguishing cases where steps can be fully implemented by generic data processing means from those requiring specific data processing means or additional technical devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See F-IV,3.9 and sub-sections 3.9.1 and 3.9.2 applied mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and interpretation of claims; invite informal clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims lack clarity, examiners may first invite the applicant to provide informal clarification before carrying out the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 5.31 and GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII, 3.3-3.6. Interpretation guidance follows ISPE Guidelines 5.20 and related appendix options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential features and objections from missing essential features
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must include essential features of the invention; missing essential features give rise to objections under clarity/support provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition, examples and treatment of essential features are given in F-IV,4.5.1-4.5.5 and Annex examples; implicit features are considered under ISPE Guidelines 5.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative terms, 'about'/'approximately', parameters and measurement methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of relative terms, 'about'/'approximately', and parametric definitions require careful treatment; the method and means for measurement of parameters may need to be included in the claim or described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See F-IV,4.6-4.7 and F-IV,4.11 and GL/PCT-EPO G-VI,6 for novelty assessment of parameter-containing claims; see GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,4.18 regarding methods of measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-process claims: interpretation and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Product-by-process claims (product defined by process) are allowable only if the product itself meets patentability requirements; novelty depends on whether the product is identical to known products, and the burden of proof that a process-modified product is distinct lies with the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims like 'Product X obtainable by process Y' are construed as claims to the product as such and confer absolute protection. Examiner must provide reasoned arguments for lack of novelty and applicant may need to provide evidence of distinguishing properties. See GL/ISPE A5.26[1] and GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,4.12 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims expressed as 'Apparatus for ...', 'Method for ...' and mixed-type claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance exists for claims directed to apparatus, methods, use and mixed/composite claims; combining incompatible claim types (e.g., combining a screening use with further production steps) may render a claim unclear under Art.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See F-IV,4.13 and examples regarding two-step claims that combine different types of process claims; Rule 6.2(a) guidance applies to such problematic combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition by reference to use or another entity; 'use' claims interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims defined by reference to use or another entity must be interpreted carefully; 'use of substance X as an insecticide' is not to be read as a claim to the substance per se but as a claim directed to the use (equivalent to a process claim for the process of using).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL/ISPE A5.21 applied by EPO; beware two-step claims combining use and production steps as these may combine irreconcilable claim types. See F-IV,4.14 and 4.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to description/drawings in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: References in claims to the description or drawings are governed by ISPE Guidelines 5.10 and Rule 6.2(b); reference signs may be used but bracketed added text or bracketed non-reference expressions can create lack of clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many embodiments exist, only reference signs of most important need be in independent claims. Bracketed features like 'securing means (screw 13)' are generally not permissible as it is unclear whether bracketed features are limiting. Acceptable forms include references to figure numbers where reference signs appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative limitations and disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative limitations (disclaimers) may exceptionally restrict subject-matter by specifying absent features; they may be used only if adding positive features would not define the subject-matter more clearly/concise or would unduly limit scope, and it must be clear what is excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims containing disclaimers must fully comply with clarity and conciseness of Art.6. Allowability of disclaimers excluding originally disclosed embodiments vs undisclosed disclaimers is treated in GL/PCT-EPO H-III (4.1-4.2). EPO applies option GL/ISPE A20.21[2].

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprising vs consisting
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctions between 'comprising' and 'consisting' and their effects on claim scope follow the EPO Guidelines and ISPE Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See F-IV,4.21 and GL/ISPE 5.24(a),(b) for application mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademarks, proper names and trade names in description and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of proper names, trademarks and trade names should comply with ISPE Guidelines 4.25; trademarks in claims raise clarity/support considerations under Art.6 and Art.5 if sufficiency is implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For assessment of clarity of claims referring to a trademark see GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,4.8; acknowledge trademarks as such in description per GL/PCT-EPO F-II,4.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional features and definition in terms of result to be achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional features and claims defined as 'result to be achieved' have special tests; defining subject-matter by result differs from functional features and may pose problems if essential features are missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See F-IV,4.9-4.10 and GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,6.5 and GL/ISPE 5.36 for allowability and related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad claims: potential objections and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Although PCT Regulations do not explicitly mention 'overly broad' claims, objections may arise for lack of support, insufficiency, novelty or inventive step if claims are formulated so broadly they cover known subject-matter or embodiments for which the purported effect has not been achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/ISPE 5.42 and GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,6.1 and G-VII,5.2 for how to handle broad claims and when to raise objections under Art.5 and Art.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and arrangement of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Although there is no legal requirement that the first claim be the broadest, claims must be clear individually and as a whole; with many claims, they should be arranged with the broadest claim first or highlight the broadest claim in introductory parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the broadest claim is not first, later broader claims must be independent. Objections under Rule 6 may arise if arrangement causes lack of clarity/conciseness. See Rule 6.1(a) and F-IV,4.24 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and number of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be concise; the EPO applies option GL/ISPE A5.42[2] regarding conciseness and number of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims lack conciseness under Art.6, the examiner may invite informal clarification before search (GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII, 3.3-3.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support in the description for claims (Art.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be fully supported by the description; the extent of generalisation permitted depends on how groundbreaking the invention is and justification by the technical contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objection of lack of support is illustrated by examples in GL/EPO F-IV,6.3; once examiner sets out a reasoned case that a claim is not supported, the onus is on applicant to demonstrate support. See ISPE Guidelines 5.43-5.53.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of support vs insufficient disclosure interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: An objection under Art.6 for lack of support may also amount to an Art.5 insufficiency objection when the disclosure does not enable the skilled person to carry out the invention across the whole claimed breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both requirements reflect that claim terms should be commensurate with the invention's technical contribution. Examples include parametric claims lacking enabling information. See GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,6 and GL/ISPE 4.12,5.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition in terms of function
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of subject-matter in functional terms is permissible in some circumstances, but requirements differ from functional features; special cases like functional definitions of pathological conditions have their own treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 5.56 and GL/PCT-EPO F-IV,2.1 and 4.10 for criteria and limitations.
